reasonToGo: Turf that burns and water that is not salt. Reedstrand's eight regions draw no rock, no scree and no karst between them, so the only stone on this head is what the sea has broken off its own platform and laid along the raised beach — and there is nowhere near enough of it to quarry. What the head does have is peat in four separate mires and a spring line at the back of the fen. One region borders this one and no road is drawn anywhere on the landmass, so a crew comes in off the water, cuts, and goes back out the way it came.

hazards.name: The quaking crust
hazards.description: One of the mires here is raised bog and another is a blanket laid over the whole back of the head. The crust carries a loaded barrow in a dry month and will not carry a man in a wet one, and what is under it is water to the depth of the peat, which nobody has sounded.

hazards.name: Nothing to found on
hazards.description: What the beach gives is loose slab off a broken platform, and there is no bedrock under any of it — none anywhere on Reedstrand to bring in either. A camp here stands on cut turf over peat, it settles unevenly through a season, and what a winter gale lifts off it does not come back.
hazards.note: Absence hazard: the harm is the missing bedrock. Nothing in the runtime enum expresses ground that will not bear a footing.

resources.name: Head turf
resources.description: Cut from the hags at the back of the head and stacked to dry on the raised beach, which is the one strip of this ground that dries at all. It is cut and not gathered: a season standing in water for a winter of burning, and a crew that starts late burns wet turf.

resources.name: Fen spring water
resources.description: Taken at the spring line where the mire meets the rising back of the head, above anything the tide reaches. It is the only fresh water drawn on this ground and it runs the whole year, which is why the cutting camps sit inland at the fen head and not on the strand where the boats are.

landmarks.name: Marramlow Carr
landmarks.description: The wet back of the head, where reed fen, wet meadow and seasonal marsh run into one another with no line between them. Nothing woody stands in it — the fabric draws no forest on any part of this ground — and it is crossed in a hard winter, when the spring line freezes stiff enough to carry a barrow, and skirted the rest of the year.

landmarks.name: Geo between Lagoonmere
landmarks.description: The one cleft in the seaward face, cut back far enough that a boat inside it is out of the weather and out of sight of the open water. The lagoon behind the bar is reached through it, and every crew that works the mires lands here rather than on the strand.
